venue.name: Courtenay and District Museum and Palaeontology Centre
venue.description: The Courtenay and District Museum and Palaeontology Centre is a non-profit museum at 207 Fourth Street in downtown Courtenay, established in 1961. Its galleries hold marine fossils from the Comox Valley, including casts of the Puntledge elasmosaur and a tylosaurus, alongside displays on local cultural history. It runs guided fossil tours out to river sites and a set of priced education programs for classes, on site, outdoors and by Zoom. Admission to the museum itself is by donation.
venue.hours_notes: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: The museum says that during early spring and late fall the fossil tours are weather dependent.

programs.name: Fossil Tour
programs.description: A guided tour that starts at the museum with a short talk about local fossil discoveries and a walk through the palaeontology galleries, then moves out to a fossil site on a local river where everyone gets to look for a fossil of their own. Hammers, chisels and goggles are supplied and you keep what you find, though the museum may ask you to donate anything of scientific value with the finder's name attached. Prices here are per person, and the museum also publishes a family rate. You have to provide your own transport between the museum and the river site.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the museum for a short talk, then walk through the fossil galleries to see the elasmosaur and other specimens. After a ten minute drive and an easy five minute walk through forest to the river, they put on goggles and use hammers and chisels to split shale and hunt for a fossil to keep.
programs.our_note: There is no bus in this. You have to arrange cars between the museum and the river for the whole group, and the museum says a vehicle is required. It runs three hours end to end and the second half is on a riverbank, so dress for weather and rough footing. Under fours come free.
programs.practical_summary: Tools and safety goggles are supplied, tours run Tuesday to Saturday at 9am or 1pm, and you pay in full when you book. Toilets, lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned anywhere, and you drive yourselves to the river.
programs.extra_fees_note: Children aged 4 to 16 are $36.75 and children under 4 are free. A family rate of $173.25 covers 2 adults and up to three children aged 4 to 16. Courtenay Museum members get 15% off all tours.
programs.payment_timing: Payment in full is required at the time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hours notice is required for refund.
programs.evidence: (2 adults and up to three children 4-16 years old)

programs.name: Private group fossil tour
programs.description: The same fossil tour booked privately for one group instead of joining a public tour. The museum publishes a single flat price for the group and describes it as covering up to 15 adults, so how a class of children is counted and charged has to be asked. Everything else matches the public tour: a talk and the galleries at the museum, then a drive and a short forest walk to a river site where tools and goggles are supplied.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the museum for a short talk, then walk through the fossil galleries. After a ten minute drive and an easy five minute walk through forest to the river, they put on goggles and use hammers and chisels to split shale and hunt for a fossil to keep.
programs.our_note: The published private rate is written for up to 15 adults and says nothing about a class of children, so that is the first thing to ask. Their school programs take up to 30 and cost less, so it is worth asking which route is cheaper for your group before you book this one.
programs.practical_summary: Three hours, starting at the museum and finishing on a riverbank, with tools and goggles supplied and payment due in full at booking. You drive yourselves to the river. Toilets, lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned.
programs.extra_fees_note: Courtenay Museum members get 15% off all tours. The published figure is written as covering up to 15 adults; the site does not say how children are counted against that.
programs.payment_timing: Payment in full is required at the time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hours notice is required for refund.

programs.name: Fossil A school program
programs.description: The museum's introductory fossil program for classes, held at the museum. It opens with an interactive discussion and presentation about the formation of Vancouver Island and the warm shallow sea that once covered it, then the group tours the palaeontology exhibits or studies fossil specimens up close. The museum recommends combining it with the river field trip, Fossil B, at a combined price. The price is published against a maximum of 30 people.
programs.what_children_do: Sit for a talk and presentation about how Vancouver Island formed and the 80 million year old sea that covered it, then move through the palaeontology galleries to look at fossil specimens close up.
programs.our_note: This is the indoors half of the fossil pair, and on its own it is looking rather than digging. If you want the children holding tools, you need Fossil B as well, and the museum prices the two together. Ask them to confirm the price in writing, because their page has carried more than one figure.
programs.practical_summary: Held at the museum, up to 30 people, and no travel involved. Duration, toilets, lunch space and bus parking are not stated, and how far ahead to book is not published.
programs.extra_fees_note: The museum highly recommends combining Fossil A and B, priced at $250.00 for a maximum of 30 people.

programs.name: Fossil B school field trip
programs.description: The museum calls this the most popular part of its fossil programs. The class is taken to the Puntledge River to explore an 80 million year old sea floor. After a short talk about what to look for, how to use the tools, safety and the history of the dig site, the children search for fossils in the shale. It can be combined with Fossil A at a combined price. The price is published against a maximum of 30 people.
programs.what_children_do: Stand and crouch on a riverbank at the Puntledge River, listen to a short briefing on tools and safety, then break and search shale for fossils.
programs.our_note: This is the one where the children have the tools in their hands, and it is outdoors on a riverbank, so plan for weather, footwear and a good number of adults. The page does not say how the group gets to the river for this program, unlike the Comox Lake one where it says you arrange your own transport, so confirm that when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors at the river, up to 30 people. Duration, transport arrangements, toilets, lunch space and how far ahead to book are all unstated, so ask before you commit.
programs.extra_fees_note: The museum highly recommends combining Fossil A and B, priced at $250.00 for a maximum of 30 people.

programs.name: Geology A school program
programs.description: A geology program for classes held at the museum. Through a presentation, hands-on activities and interactive discussion the children compare geological features and look at the cause and effect of natural formations. The museum recommends combining it with Geology B, the field trip to Comox Lake, at a combined price. The price is published against a maximum of 30 people.
programs.what_children_do: Sit for a presentation about the changing surface of the earth, then take part in hands-on activities and discussion comparing rocks and landforms.
programs.our_note: This is the classroom style half, done at the museum. If you want the children outside handling rocks in the field, you need Geology B too, and the museum prices the pair together.
programs.practical_summary: Held at the museum, up to 30 people, no travel involved. Duration, toilets, lunch space and bus parking are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: The museum highly recommends combining Geology A and B, priced at $250.00 for a maximum of 30 people.

programs.name: Geology B school field trip
programs.description: An extension of Geology A that takes the class to a geologically significant site at Comox Lake, where the children examine rocks, minerals and formations and watch the processes of sedimentation, erosion and volcanic activity. The museum states plainly that the group provides its own transport to and from Comox Lake, by parent, car pool or bus. The price is published against a maximum of 30 people.
programs.what_children_do: Walk a site at Comox Lake, pick up and examine different rocks and minerals, and look at layers and formations in the ground to work out how they formed.
programs.our_note: You arrange the ride to Comox Lake yourselves, which the museum says can be parents, a car pool or a bus. That is the part that takes the planning, so sort it before you fix a date. Everything else happens outdoors, so watch the weather.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors at Comox Lake, up to 30 people, with your own transport there and back. Duration, toilets, lunch space and lead time are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: The museum highly recommends combining Geology A and B, priced at $250.00 for a maximum of 30 people. The group must provide its own transportation from the museum to and from Comox Lake, either by parent, car pool or bus.

programs.name: Early Colonial Settlement school program
programs.description: An hour and a half program at the museum about the changes in family life in the Comox Valley brought about by new technology and early colonial settlement, set against the thousands of years K'omoks First Nation had lived on their territory beforehand. It includes a slide show introduction to Comox Valley history, a tour of the exhibits, and an interactive session with artifacts and an activity. Clothing, tools, food, education, housekeeping and entertainment, past and present, are examined through hands-on experiences. The price is published against a maximum of 30.
programs.what_children_do: Watch a short slide show, walk the exhibits, then sit with real artifacts and handle clothing, tools and household objects while comparing them with what they use now.
programs.our_note: An hour and a half is the longest of the museum programs and most of it is sitting and handling objects, which suits a settled group better than a restless one. It is the one to pick if you want local history rather than fossils.
programs.practical_summary: Ninety minutes at the museum, up to 30 people, with artifacts to handle. Toilets, lunch space, bus parking and how far ahead to book are not stated.

programs.name: General Tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the whole museum combining natural and cultural history, which the museum says is pitched at all age levels. It runs between one and one and a half hours, through presentation and walking commentary, and covers what the museum has across its galleries. The price is published against a maximum of 30 people.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the museum galleries with a guide talking as they go, seeing both the fossil collection and the local history displays.
programs.our_note: This is the one the museum describes as suiting all ages, so it is the safest choice for a mixed or very young group. It is walking and listening rather than doing, so keep it to the shorter end if the children are small.
programs.practical_summary: One to one and a half hours at the museum, up to 30 people, all indoors. Toilets, lunch space, bus parking and lead time are not stated.
programs.evidence: This tour combines natural and cultural history for all age levels.

programs.name: Fossil and geology sessions by Zoom
programs.description: One hour interactive sessions delivered to the classroom by Zoom with the museum's Earth Science Curator. Two topics are offered at the same price: Fossil A, an introduction to prehistoric life in the Comox Valley with a Zoom tour of the palaeontology exhibits and a chance to study specimens up close and ask questions, and Geology A, a discussion of regional geology with a tour of the museum gallery. Booking is by phone.
programs.what_children_do: Stay in their own room and watch a presentation and a live tour of the museum galleries on screen, looking at fossil specimens held up close to the camera and asking the curator questions.
programs.our_note: This is the option with no travel and no weather in it, which matters for a group too young for a riverbank. One hour is about right for a screen, and it is the only offering the museum gives a firm length for.
programs.practical_summary: One hour, delivered to your room by Zoom, booked by phone. Nothing else is needed at your end beyond a screen and a connection. Group size, ages and lead time are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Fossil A and Geology A are each $150.00 for a one hour session.
programs.evidence: Please phone 250-334-0686 to book a one-hour interactive session.

gaps: PER-GROUP READING IS AN INFERENCE: the education programs page prints a bare figure followed by a maximum, for example $150.00 (Maximum 30 persons). It never uses the words per class, per group or per student. We recorded these as a flat price for the whole group because per student would come to $4,500 for a class of 30, but the site does not say so. Confirm it in writing before you book, because at a class of 22 the difference is thousands of dollars.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: plain fetching this site returned an out of date copy of the education programs page showing $120.00 plus GST prices and an extra program called the Courtenay Riverway Walk at $140.00 plus GST. The live page in a browser shows $150.00 and $180.00 with no tax line and no Riverway Walk. All prices here were read from the live page. A fetch-only re-run will silently reinstate the old prices.
no ages or grades are published for any program; the fossil tour prices children as 4 to 16 with under 4s free, but that is a price band rather than a stated age range, so no age band is recorded
whether the school program prices include tax is not stated on the live page; the earlier version of the same page showed the same programs at a lower figure plus GST, so ask whether tax is on top
no price year or season is published, so how current the school program prices are cannot be established from the page itself
no lead time or minimum notice for any school program; the fossil tour says only that pre-booking is required
no washrooms, lunch space, rain backup, stroller access, wheelchair access or bus parking information anywhere on the site
no chaperone ratio for any program
no duration published for Fossil A, Fossil B, Geology A or Geology B
Fossil B does not say who arranges transport to the Puntledge River, although Geology B says plainly that the group arranges its own transport to Comox Lake
no capacity published for the group programmes route or for the Zoom sessions
the map embed on their directions page carries only the map viewport centre and no place pin, so the point was derived from the published street address instead
the site's Open Graph image is the museum logo rather than a photograph, so the hero is the river photograph from the home page; the site publishes no exterior photograph of the building
alt text for both images was written by us after opening the image files in a browser and looking at them; neither image has an alt attribute on the site

conflicts.note: Their school programs page has been showing two different prices, an older one of about $120 plus tax and a current one of $150 for a group of up to 30. The $150 is what the page shows now. Get the price confirmed in writing when you book.

The fossil tour price has been shown two ways, once as $36.75 for a child and once as $35 with tax added on top to reach the same total. Either way it comes to $36.75 a child, but ask whether tax is included so there is no surprise.
